subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these cities is a megacity in a newly emerging economy (NEE)?
questions.explain: Mumbai is a rapidly growing megacity in India, a newly emerging economy.

questions.q: Which of these is a social challenge linked to rapid urban growth?
options: Inequality between rich and poor districts
questions.explain: Rapid urban growth often widens inequality, with wealthy areas alongside deprived slums lacking services.

questions.q: One way to improve a squatter settlement is through 'site and service' schemes, which:
options: Move all residents to rural areas
Provide land with basic utilities so residents can build better homes
questions.explain: Site and service schemes give people a plot connected to water and electricity, allowing them to gradually self-build improved housing.

questions.q: Which of these is a common challenge caused by rapid urban growth in LICs and NEEs?
options: Too few people to fill jobs
questions.explain: Rapid growth can overwhelm services such as water, sanitation and transport, leading to congestion and pollution.

questions.q: What is a 'squatter settlement' (slum)?
options: An area of poor-quality housing built illegally on unused land
A planned suburb with large houses
questions.explain: Squatter settlements, such as favelas, are areas of self-built, often illegal housing that lack basic services.

questions.q: Recycling household waste and using renewable energy in a city helps make it more sustainable by:
options: Reducing waste and lowering carbon emissions
questions.explain: Recycling cuts the waste sent to landfill and renewable energy lowers carbon emissions, improving sustainability.

questions.q: Encouraging people to cycle, walk and use trams instead of cars mainly helps a city by:
questions.explain: Integrated, low-carbon transport reduces congestion and air pollution, making the city more sustainable.

questions.q: In many UK cities, old industrial dockland areas have been regenerated mainly to:
options: Create new housing, offices and leisure facilities
questions.explain: Regeneration of derelict docklands, such as in London or Liverpool, creates modern housing, business and leisure spaces.

questions.q: Which of the following is an opportunity created by urban growth?
options: Greater access to jobs, services and education
questions.explain: Cities concentrate employment, education and healthcare, giving residents better access to opportunities than rural areas.

questions.q: Heavy traffic congestion in a growing city mainly leads to:
options: Air pollution and longer journey times
A fall in the city's population
questions.explain: Congestion increases air pollution from exhaust fumes and wastes time, harming health and the economy.

questions.q: Which of these is a 'push' factor encouraging rural-to-urban migration?
options: Entertainment and shops in the city
Good schools and hospitals in the city
Lack of services and poverty in the countryside
questions.explain: Push factors drive people away from an area, such as rural poverty, drought and a lack of services.

questions.q: A 'green belt' around a UK city is an area of land that is:
options: Protected from most building to limit urban sprawl
questions.explain: A green belt is protected open land around a city that restricts development and helps prevent urban sprawl.

questions.q: Building on previously developed 'brownfield' sites within a city helps sustainability because it:
options: Reuses derelict land and protects greenfield sites
questions.explain: Brownfield development reuses abandoned urban land, reducing pressure to build on undeveloped greenfield countryside.

questions.q: Which of these is a 'pull' factor attracting people to cities?
questions.explain: Pull factors attract people to an area, such as the prospect of jobs, schools, hospitals and a higher standard of living.

questions.q: Why do many people in LIC/NEE cities work in the 'informal' economy?
options: The government requires it by law
They cannot find formal, regulated jobs
It offers high wages and pensions
questions.explain: With too few formal jobs, many migrants do unregulated, low-paid informal work such as street selling to survive.

questions.q: Besides migration, what is the other main cause of urban population growth?
options: Natural increase, where births exceed deaths
questions.explain: Cities often have a young population, so a high birth rate combined with a lower death rate causes natural increase.

questions.q: Which of these is a feature of a sustainable city?
options: Efficient public transport and plenty of green space
questions.explain: Sustainable cities promote public transport, recycling, green spaces and renewable energy to reduce their environmental impact.

questions.q: A megacity is usually defined as a city with a population of more than:
questions.explain: A megacity is an urban area with a population of over 10 million people.

questions.q: Which statement about megacities is correct today?
options: Most megacities are now in richer, developed countries
An increasing number of the world's megacities are in LICs and NEEs
There are no megacities in Asia
questions.explain: Megacity growth is now fastest in LICs and NEEs, with many of the largest cities found in Asia and Africa.

questions.q: What is the main reason rural-urban migration leads to rapid city growth in many LICs and NEEs?
options: Birth rates in cities are extremely low
Cities are losing population to the countryside
People move from countryside to city seeking jobs and a better life
City death rates are higher than rural ones
questions.explain: Large numbers of people migrate from rural areas to cities in search of work, services and opportunities, swelling urban populations.

questions.q: Why do many of the wealthier residents in UK cities live in the suburbs rather than the inner city?
options: There are no roads in the inner city
Suburbs often have more space, greener surroundings and newer housing
Suburbs are the cheapest place to live
Inner cities have no jobs at all
questions.explain: Suburbs typically offer larger, newer homes with gardens and a quieter environment, attracting wealthier families.

questions.q: In a typical urban land-use pattern, which area is usually found at the centre of a city?
questions.explain: The CBD is the commercial heart of a city, with shops and offices, usually located in the centre where land is most accessible.
